title: STILL PRESENT (r1) W3: stale-bounce gate broken for same-day redeliveries — lexical compare mixes RFC3339 'T'-format with Postgres space-format ::text
evidence: SQL: `COALESCE((SELECT e->>'at' FROM jsonb_array_elements(rc.attempts) AS e WHERE e->>'detail' = $4 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered' ORDER BY e->>'at' DESC LIMIT 1), '') AS matched_send_at,` and `COALESCE(rc.corrected_at::text, '') AS corrected_at,`; sweep writes at via `|> timestamp.to_rfc3339(calendar.utc_offset)` (sweep.gleam:180); handler: `// ISO timestamps — lexical compare is chronological.` `string.compare(at, corrected) != order.Lt` (webhooks.gleam:303-304)
detail: at is RFC3339 ('2026-08-09T08:00:00Z'), corrected_at::text is Postgres space format ('2026-08-09 12:00:00+00'). Same-date pairs always sort at>corrected ('T' 0x54 vs ' ' 0x20) regardless of time, so a redelivered PRE-correction bounce on correction day is classified genuine and exhausts the corrected row with a fabricated referee_contact_invalid — W3's exact threat, in the window redeliveries actually land. Both tests pin only cross-day shapes.
recommended_fix: Emit both timestamps in one format (CAST e->>'at' AS timestamptz in SQL, or to_char corrected_at to RFC3339) and compare chronologically; pin a same-day stale-bounce stand-down test.

title: Exhaustion path lacks taken_over_at guard — a late bounce or wrong-person response terminalizes a row the landlord is handling
evidence: `WHERE id = $1` / `  AND status IN ('queued', 'contact_initiated')` / `RETURNING id::text;` — no taken_over_at clause; same-PR writers all gained it: sweep_claim_t0.sql `AND taken_over_at IS NULL`, sweep_advance.sql `AND taken_over_at IS NULL`, rearm_queued_reference_calls.sql `AND taken_over_at IS NULL`, sweep_due_reference_calls.sql `AND rc.taken_over_at IS NULL`; take-over writes only taken_over_at + next_attempt_at=NULL, never status (take_over_reference_call.sql), so a taken-over row keeps status queued/contact_initiated; form link stays live after take-over (§8.6) and the wrong-person route calls exhaust_reference_call for correction_cycles >= 1 (form_handler.gleam:1275)
detail: Take-over leaves status queued/contact_initiated, so the webhook exhaust_row and the wrong-person route both pass the status-only guard: the row terminalizes unreachable + permanent referee_contact_invalid stamp + in-app notification while the landlord is actively handling it. Every other automated writer in this PR excludes taken-over rows; this new terminal does not.
recommended_fix: Add AND taken_over_at IS NULL to exhaust_reference_call.sql's WHERE (symmetric with the claim/advance/rearm guards) and pin a test: exhaustion on a taken-over row stands down without stamp.

title: STILL PRESENT (r1) N11: concurrent substitute double-submit can still return 409 instead of the documented 200 idempotent no-op
evidence: `ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (...) DO NOTHING` + `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted);` — the 'existing' SELECT runs with the statement's READ COMMITTED snapshot; handler 0-row branch: `Ok(pog.Returned(_, [])) -> Error(NotSubstitutable)` (actions_handler.gleam:361)
detail: Sequential double-submit returns 'existing' 200 (pinned). Truly concurrent double-submit: the loser's INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waits for the winner, but the statement snapshot predates the winner's commit, so the 'existing' SELECT cannot see the committed successor — 0 rows, 409. No serialization was added.
recommended_fix: Serialize the idempotent CTE (pg_advisory_xact_lock on the slot key) or re-run the statement once on 0 rows; add a two-connection concurrent double-submit test asserting 200 + one audit.
